source.title: What Can Grokking Teach Us About Learning Under Nonstationarity?
source.authors: Clare Lyle; Ghada Sokar; Razvan Pascanu; András Gyorgy

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present, though several plotted results are represented only by flattened figure content
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests grokking on modular addition using learning-rate and parameter-norm interventions, and measures test accuracy and feature changes; it does not reproduce the original training recipe unchanged.
record.gate_note: The paper's own modular-arithmetic experiments bear on grokking, feature-learning measures, and the role of parameter norm. It does not test dataset-size-dependent delays, algorithm identity, LLM training, or optimizer/numerical-artifact explanations. Results cited from prior work are not recorded as rows. The warm-start image and reinforcement-learning experiments concern adaptation/generalization in different settings, not spontaneous delayed generalization of the kind specified in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper trains its own one-block transformers on modular addition (mod 117, ρ=0.2). It varies learning rate, weight decay, norm projection, layer norm and scale decay, and reports when test accuracy rises after training accuracy saturates. The results bear on V1 (delayed generalization), V3 (an ELR, i.e. update-to-norm ratio, switch with feature learning) and V5 (whether norm reduction is what drives grokking). It uses a different method from the originals and is not one of them. The CIFAR warm-start and Atari sections are not grokking.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also state that the effective learning rate, not parameter norm on its own, drives grokking. They add that feature learning alone is insufficient: generalization also needs a loss landscape in which the feature changes converge to a smooth solution. They frame grokking as a model for overcoming primacy bias in continual learning.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a modular-addition transformer setting, but focuses on effective-learning-rate rewarming, parameter renormalization, and scale decay rather than reproducing the original grokking training method unchanged.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with learning rate, parameter-norm constraint, layer normalization, and decay applied to normalization scale parameters.

fits_no_version.finding: Grokking frequently coincides with a drop in attention-output rank. With LN, reducing that rank requires reducing attention-input or key/query norms (Fig. 8, App. B.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking coincides with a reduction in attention-output rank.

record.problems: The paper does not report uncertainty estimates for the modular-arithmetic results, and numeric values for many accuracy and feature-measure curves are not recoverable from the flattened figure text. The grokking experiment uses a single stated training fraction, so it does not establish the claimed relationship between training-set size and delay.
record.rows_left_out: Warm-start image-classification and reinforcement-learning results were left out because they report adaptation or task performance, not the delayed generalization behavior specified by the tested versions. The per-condition plotted values in Figures 2–3 and Figure 8 could not be separately assigned from the flattened figure text; rows record only outcomes explicitly described in the prose or captions.

untested.parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks; only ρ=0.2 is used.
All of it: no Fourier or circuit identification, no tracking of memorization removal, and no progress measure shown to anticipate the jump.
Grokking on non-algorithmic data (the CIFAR warm-start is not delayed generalization) and switching via initialization scale.
Circuit efficiency, critical dataset size, and ungrokking.
All; Adam is used throughout, with no optimizer or numerical controls.

missing.what: Test-accuracy floor of about 20% from input symmetry, with some networks dropping below it before grokking. This is relevant to what 'chance' means in V1.
Fig. 2 right panel distinguishes decay values of 1.0 and 10.0 with and without scale decay; per-condition outcomes are not recorded.

record.verdict_notes: There are no uncertainty estimates, and the curves are only plotted. Grokking is deliberately induced by LR schedules, but the low-ELR settings show the delay arising without intervention. Training-set size is never varied for modular arithmetic, and the dataset-size variation in Fig. 4 is CIFAR warm-starting, not grokking.

versions.untested_parts: Whether the delay grows as the training set shrinks; the experiments use a ρ = 0.2 train split for the modular task rather than a training-set-size sweep.

The paper measures feature covariance, activation-pattern change, and attention-output rank, but does not identify a Fourier algorithm, track removal of memorizing components, or establish that a continuous progress measure anticipates the test-accuracy jump.
The paper tests learning-rate and norm manipulations in modular arithmetic, but not efficient-circuit formation, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below a dataset-size threshold.

rows.subject: transformer with a single attention block
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular addition and evaluate on held-out input pairs
rows.measure: training and test accuracy over training
rows.value: Almost all networks attain perfect or near-perfect training accuracy typically within one thousand steps; the paper reports delayed test generalization in the grokking settings, with curve values shown in figures.
rows.note: Training accuracy is explicitly described but not plotted. The paper does not provide extractable numerical test-accuracy values for the curves.
rows.check: Training accuracy saturates within about 1000 steps and test accuracy rises later in the low-ELR curves of Fig. 2. No numbers are given. The baseline should be about 20% test accuracy from the (x,y)/(y,x) symmetry (App. A.1), not chance at 1/117.

rows.subject: transformer with a single attention block
rows.operation_detail: Sweep learning rate and weight decay while allowing parameter norm to vary
rows.measure: test accuracy and onset of grokking
rows.value: The text says learning rate has a stronger effect on grokking than weight-decay value in variable-norm networks; larger weight decay can compensate for smaller learning rate.
rows.note: The paper describes the sweep-level finding but does not give extractable curve values for each learning-rate/weight-decay combination.
rows.check: For V5, weight decay matters, but less than learning rate, and larger weight decay can compensate for a smaller learning rate. For V1 and V3, the onset of grokking shifts with ELR. This is a sweep-level description with no per-condition values.

source_check.correct: The sweep establishes regime-dependent grokking and a stronger learning-rate effect than weight-decay effect. A single partial state does not describe all linked versions: grokking is observed in successful conditions; generalizing-circuit efficiency is not measured.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1; Figure 2 caption and paragraph immediately following Figure 3.
source_check.problem: The partial state conflates a sweep-level dependence with incomplete occurrence and an unmeasured efficiency mechanism.

rows.subject: transformer with a single attention block
rows.operation_detail: Periodically rescale parameters to their original norm during the learning-rate and weight-decay sweep
rows.measure: test accuracy and consistency of generalization across random seeds
rows.value: Periodic weight projection is reported to produce rapid and consistent generalization across random seeds; the text says it blunts the effect of weight decay.
rows.note: Individual curve values are not extractable from the figure text.
rows.check: State refers to V5. Rapid, seed-consistent grokking occurs while the norm is held near its initial value, so norm reduction is not needed here. For V3 the row is observed: ELR set by fixed norm and learning rate switches grokking on. It should not be linked to V1, since it shows rapid rather than delayed generalization.

source_check.correct: Observed regime-controlled grokking for V3. For V5, circuit efficiency cannot be determined: rapid generalization at approximately fixed parameter norm establishes that norm reduction is unnecessary here, not that efficient generalizing circuits or low-norm biases are absent.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1; Figure 2 left panels and caption; paragraph immediately following Figure 3.
source_check.problem: Absent is not justified for the efficiency mechanism, which the experiment does not measure.

rows.subject: transformer with layer normalization and periodic parameter renormalization
rows.operation_detail: Train with parameter renormalization and no scale decay
rows.value: The authors state that weight normalization completely fails to generalize in this architecture.
rows.note: The paper attributes the failure to layer normalization producing large attention inputs and difficult-to-optimize, low-entropy attention.
rows.check: With layer norm, a high ELR under projection produces no generalization, so the ELR/norm switch fails in this architecture. Not a V1 or V2 measurement.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1, final paragraph; Figure 2 right panels and caption.

rows.subject: transformer with layer normalization and periodic parameter renormalization
rows.operation_detail: Apply weight decay to layer-normalization scale parameters
rows.value: The authors report generalization after applying scale decay; the plotted curves are not numerically extractable.
rows.note: The paper concludes that meaningful representation change alone is insufficient without a suitable loss landscape.
rows.check: Generalization returns only when decay is applied to the layer-norm scales. That is a norm reduction, but the authors attribute it to attention entropy and smoothness, not circuit efficiency. No V2 content.

source_check.correct: Scale decay restores generalization under projection with layer normalization. The regime-dependent switch is observed for V3; V5 circuit efficiency cannot be determined. The authors explain the scale-decay requirement through attention-input magnitude, attention entropy and optimization smoothness.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1, final paragraph; Figure 2 right panels and caption.
source_check.problem: Partial does not describe restored generalization and does not establish a partially observed efficiency mechanism.

rows.subject: transformer with layer normalization and periodic parameter renormalization
rows.operation_detail: Increase the effective learning rate to induce grokking, with a low-learning-rate comparison

conditions.value: linear warmup followed by cosine decay

rows.value: The text reports rapidly obtaining perfect test accuracy, which persists after one million optimizer steps.
rows.note: The curve values are not numerically extractable.
rows.check: State refers to V3: warming the ELR to 0.01 switches on rapid perfect test accuracy. For V1 this is a shortened delay, a scope condition. Not V2.

source_check.correct: The Figure 3 protocol includes weight projection, layer normalization and scale decay. Linear warmup to learning rate 0.01 followed by cosine decay rapidly produces perfect test accuracy, retained after one million optimizer steps. Observed applies to the V3 switch; the V1 delay is shortened.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, first paragraph; Figure 3 caption; Appendix A.1.
source_check.problem: The condition omits scale decay, an essential component of the reported layer-normalized protocol.

rows.subject: transformer with layer normalization and periodic parameter renormalization
rows.operation_detail: Measure activation-pattern change during learning-rate rewarming

conditions.value: linear warmup followed by cosine decay

rows.value: The figure and its caption report that increasing the learning rate to 0.01 leads to feature learning and grokking.
rows.note: No numeric activation-pattern-change value is stated in the text.
rows.check: Activation-pattern change, a lazy-to-rich proxy, accompanies grokking at LR 0.01. It is not a progress measure shown to anticipate the jump, so it is not V2. numbers_found of 1/1 is unexplained; no numeric value exists.

source_check.correct: Figure 3 uses weight projection, layer normalization and scale decay. Rewarming to learning rate 0.01 produces activation-pattern change and grokking; no numerical activation-change percentage is stated.
source_check.problem: The condition omits scale decay from the Figure 3 protocol.

rows.subject: transformer with layer normalization and periodic parameter renormalization
rows.operation_detail: Compare a lower learning-rate condition that does not induce grokking
rows.value: The figure caption states that increasing the learning rate to 0.001 does not produce feature learning or grokking.
rows.note: The text does not provide numeric values for either measure.
rows.check: This control confirms the switch: rewarming only to 0.001 gives no feature learning and no grokking. Its state relative to V3 is observed, not absent.

source_check.correct: The lower-rate comparison uses weight projection, layer normalization and scale decay. Rewarming to 0.001 fails to induce feature learning and grokking, unlike rewarming to 0.01.
source_check.problem: The condition omits scale decay from the Figure 3 protocol.

rows.subject: transformer with layer normalization and periodic parameter renormalization
rows.operation_detail: Delay the start of the effective-learning-rate schedule, then rewarm

conditions.value: varied; Figure 3 labels 20000 and 100000, and the text describes delays of several hundred thousand optimizer steps

rows.baseline: training at a learning rate too low to induce grokking before rewarming
rows.value: The authors report that grokking can still be induced after several hundred thousand optimizer steps of prior training.
rows.note: Individual outcomes for each delay are not numerically extractable.
rows.check: Grokking is induced after several hundred thousand low-LR steps (Fig. 3 shows 20k, 100k and 500k offsets). Here the delay is set by the LR schedule.

source_check.correct: The delayed-rewarming protocol includes weight projection, layer normalization and scale decay. Figure 3 labels offsets of 0, 20000, 100000 and 500000 steps; Section 4.2 reports successful induction after several hundred thousand low-rate steps.
source_check.problem: The condition omits scale decay; the listed offsets are supported.

rows.subject: transformer with layer normalization and periodic parameter renormalization
rows.operation_detail: Track attention-output rank in modular-arithmetic runs

conditions.value: layer normalization and periodic parameter renormalization

rows.measure: rank of attention outputs over training
rows.value: The authors state that grokking frequently coincides with a reduction in attention-output rank.
rows.note: This is a qualitative association; the paper does not establish that the rank measure precedes the test-accuracy increase.
rows.check: Attention-output rank reduction coincides with grokking, but the study does not show it precedes the jump, and it is not the generalizing circuit or the removal of memorization. Moved to fits_no_version.

relationships.reason: Training accuracy saturates within about 1000 steps while test accuracy rises much later, including after long low-LR offsets (r1, r9).
relationships.display_finding: Training accuracy saturated within approximately 1,000 steps, while test accuracy rose much later, including after long low-learning-rate offsets.

relationships.condition: High ELR via LR warmup with norm projection
relationships.reason: The delay largely disappears: test accuracy becomes rapidly perfect, so the delay's length depends on the LR/norm choice (r6).

source_check.condition: High ELR via LR warmup with norm projection
source_check.reason: Section 4.2 reports rapid perfect test accuracy under rewarming, qualifying the long-delay behavior. This layer-normalized condition also requires scale decay.

relationships.condition: Modular addition, no-LN transformer, or LN with scale decay
relationships.reason: Raising the ELR (LR relative to parameter norm) switches on feature learning and grokking, and a low ELR leaves both off (r2, r3, r6, r7, r8, r9).
relationships.display_finding: Raising learning rate relative to parameter norm enabled feature learning and grokking, whereas a low ratio left both absent.

source_check.condition: Modular addition, no-LN transformer, or LN with scale decay
source_check.reason: The experiments support the training-regime and lazy-to-rich component: sufficiently high ELR induces feature learning and grokking, whereas the lower-rate control does not. Non-algorithmic grokking is untested.

relationships.condition: Transformer with layer normalization and projection, no scale decay
relationships.reason: A high ELR does not produce generalization unless attention-input norms are also reduced, so the switch depends on architecture (r4, r5).
relationships.display_finding: High effective learning rates alone failed to produce generalization; attention-input norms also had to decrease.

source_check.condition: Transformer with layer normalization and projection, no scale decay
source_check.reason: High ELR under projection fails to generalize with layer normalization unless attention-input scale is also reduced.

relationships.condition: No-LN transformer with periodic norm projection
relationships.reason: Grokking is rapid and consistent while the norm stays near its initial value, and projection blunts the effect of weight decay (r3).
relationships.display_finding: Grokking was rapid and consistent while norm remained near its initial value, and projection reduced the effect of weight decay.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: No-LN transformer with periodic norm projection
source_check.reason: Fixed-norm grokking qualifies explanations requiring parameter-norm reduction. It does not demonstrate the absence or reversal of efficient-circuit selection; both weight-decay settings remain positive and circuit efficiency is unmeasured.

relationships.condition: Variable-norm networks, and LN networks needing scale decay
relationships.reason: Weight decay helps, but the learning rate has the stronger effect, and the norm reduction needed with LN is explained by attention entropy rather than circuit efficiency (r2, r5).
relationships.display_finding: Weight decay helped less than learning rate, and attention entropy explained the norm reduction required with layer normalization.

relation.reason: The study measures delayed generalization and its dependence on learning rate, weight decay, projection and normalization.

tranche.reason: Own modular-addition experiments test grokking through effective-learning-rate interventions, parameter projection and normalization controls.

source_check.notes: Appendix A.1 gives an approximately 20% symmetry-only test baseline; this is not random-chance accuracy. The authors’ conclusion is represented accurately, but circuit efficiency, training-fraction scaling and non-algorithmic grokking are not directly tested.

statements.correction: Modulus 117; weight projection; layer normalization; scale decay; linear warmup followed by cosine decay; rapid perfect test accuracy; V1 limits_scope for this accelerated condition.
statements.problem: Rapid generalization is supported, but the challenges label overstates this condition-dependent shortening of delay. The layer-normalized rewarming protocol also includes scale decay.

statements.correction: No-layer-normalization transformer; modulus 117; renormalization every 100 steps; rapid consistent generalization near initial norm; weaker decay dependence under projection; stronger learning-rate effect with variable norm; layer-normalized projection requires scale decay; V5 limits_scope concerning norm-reduction necessity.
statements.problem: The experimental summary is supported, but challenges overstates what fixed-norm grokking establishes about circuit efficiency. No efficient-versus-memorizing circuit comparison, critical dataset size or ungrokking test is reported.
